issues.description: The script uses GM_xmlhttpRequest to communicate with ffscouter.com, which is a third-party server. This may transmit user data or page context, depending on request payloads.
issues.location: Network requests to ffscouter.com via GM_xmlhttpRequest
issues.recommendation: Review all transmitted data to ensure no sensitive or personal information is sent. Document what is sent and why. Consider user consent.

issues.description: The script requests the unsafeWindow permission, which exposes the page context to the userscript and increases the risk of privilege escalation or data leakage.
issues.recommendation: Remove unsafeWindow unless strictly necessary. If required, minimize its usage and audit all interactions with page context.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission, which is necessary for cross-origin requests, but should be limited to only required domains.
issues.recommendation: Ensure only required domains are listed in @connect and that requests are strictly controlled.

issues.description: The script loads a large block of CSS as a string and injects it into the page. While not inherently dangerous, if the CSS string is ever replaced with dynamic content, it could become a vector for DOM-based XSS.
issues.recommendation: Ensure only static, trusted CSS is injected. Do not allow user input or external data to be injected as CSS.

summary: The script transmits data to a third-party server (ffscouter.com) using GM_xmlhttpRequest, which is a critical risk if sensitive user data is sent. It also requests unsafeWindow, increasing the risk of privilege escalation. No evidence of privacy-invasive data collection, code obfuscation, or DOM XSS was found in the provided code. Permissions are mostly appropriate, but should be reviewed. Supply chain risk is low as no @require is used. Overall, the script poses a HIGH risk due to data transmission and privilege escalation potential.
